Folks — I took the security/ops questions and started filling the spreadsheet. Below are the short answers to items they call out; I attached runbook excerpts and the last BCP test summary.

Selected answers / evidence notes:
- RTO / RPO: Hosted API RTO (regional failover): aim for < 60 minutes for control-plane failover, median observed failover ~12 minutes during last cross-region exercise; RPO for user request processing: sub-second for in-flight token loss with prefix/KV cache fallback; Dedicated (pinned capacity) RTO: 4 hours for full cluster rebuild, typical warm-failover < 2 hours with snapshot + hot-standby for committed clusters.
- Cross-region failover: automatic routing via smart routing layer + health checks; active passive model with automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if exact model shard unavailable. Mean time to failover measured 10–15 minutes in last test; see BCP_Test_Report_2025-11.pdf.
- Backup cadence and retention: daily snapshots of model weights and config; KV/prefix caches are ephemeral (replayed on warm start) — long-term backups (model artifacts) retained per agreement, default 90 days; encrypted at rest with AES-256.
- Key management: we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS and HSM-backed KMS integrations; rotation: configurable, we rotate platform keys quarterly; for CMKs rotation is customer-controlled and we store only encrypted blobs; we can provide KMS ARN and rotation schedule as requested.
- Network / segmentation: control plane isolated from customer compute; Dedicated clusters run in isolated tenant VLANs with firewall ACLs. We do not co-locate customer-dedicated GPUs with other tenants. Diagram attached.

Attachments: DR_Runbook_excerpt.pdf, BCP_Test_Report_2025-11.pdf

Neha — I updated the product/architecture answers and attached the infra diagram link + short descriptions for each questionnaire row referencing the diagram. Summary below (pulled into the spreadsheet):

Product/architecture highlights:
- Isolation: Dedicated clusters are tenant-isolated with hardware pinning; VPC/private deployments place the inference worker network inside customer-controlled subnets.
- Backups & model versioning: Model artifacts are snapshotted daily; we store immutable model versions and support pinning to a model digest to ensure reproducible outputs. Backups are encrypted and we retain model artifacts 90 days by default, configurable via contract.
- Runtime resilience: Our runtime supports continuous batching and KV-cache replay. On node failure, requests are drained and routed; cached context is reconstructed from recent interaction logs where permitted. For high-availability customers we recommend hot-standby clusters with async replication (reduces RTO to under 2 hours).
- Failover & canary rollouts: Canary deploys use mirrored traffic and automatic rollback on regressions; rollouts preserve KV cache by migrating active shards where possible and issuing soft-failover to compatible quantized variants when needed.

Data residency / EU-only processing: We can commit to EU-only processing for sensitive data if the customer purchases Dedicated or our Private VPC deployment and specifies the geo constraint in the contract. Hosted tenants default to regional routing; we will work with procurement on contract language.

Attachments / links: Redwood_Infra_Diagram_v3.png (attached), diagram link: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/infra-diagram-MID-004
